relevance_note: Letter reporting 'a Japanese family containing two cases of autoinflammatory disease which exhibit an identical novel TNFAIP3 mutation' (proband and younger sister), with parental testing and functional work.
method_note: Read the whole paper manually; values were typed into a small Python builder script (no table transcription; the paper has no tables in the Markdown, and Additional file 1 / Table S1 and the Fig. 1 pedigree image are not available). Four individuals recorded: the proband (17-year-old boy at referral), his younger sister (variant carrier, affected), his mother (affected, deceased of septicaemia, genotype not reported), and his father (unaffected, Sanger-negative). Not recorded as rows: 'the younger brothers of the proband without symptoms' (plural, number not stated, not sequenced), to avoid inventing or merging people. Contradictions in the paper: (1) the nucleotide change is given as 'C596_598 del A' in the main text but as 'c597-598 T deletion' in the Fig. 1 legend; the main-text string was used for cdna_hgvs_as_stated; (2) the variant is called a frameshift ('Cys200Alafsx16; C200Afs*16', 'the frameshift mutation') but also 'a novel heterozygous missense mutation'; variant_type recorded as frameshift; (3) labs: 'There were no abnormalities except elevated levels of C-reactive protein (CRP)' yet ANA was positive at low titre and cytokines were elevated. Proband age: the only age given is '17-year-old' at referral, followed by an admission 'Three years later', so age at last evaluation is recorded as not reported. Onset 'at 14 years old' appears in a sentence about 'our patients' without naming the person; attributed to the proband because it matches his 3-year history at age 17 and the sister's onset is separately stated as 11 years. Inheritance 'inherited maternal' reflects the authors' own inference ('suggesting that these mutations were maternally derived') from a negative father; the mother's genotype is not reported. Functional (immunoblot) evidence was obtained in the proband's PBMCs and is repeated on the sister's row because it concerns the same variant. Checklist: proband 'uveitis' was excluded in phenotypic_features but 'uveitis or other ocular inflammation' left not reported (narrow absence does not exclude broad item). Sister has only 'similar symptoms' and 'suspected of Behçet’s disease', so no feature rows and all checklist items not reported. 'Neither genital ulcer nor uveitis was confirmed' on examination was read as an explicit absence.
